# NavigationOverlayKit integration for route instructions (2026-01-30 16:27Z)

_**User**_

when the user starts the navigation towards a device the route FROM the device towards the user is shown. At any point in time the user can switch the routes by pushing the switch button at the top to FROM his device towards the other device.

When the navigation is switched to the mode "from the current device towards the other device" I want to display navigation instructions and to do that use the https://github.com/bietiekay/NavigationOverlayKit  NavigationOverlayKit Framework.

Make a plan to implement this behaviour with all side effects and eventualities as well as changes to documentation, changelot etc.

miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## App Navigation and Views\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\\\\\\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\\\\\\\\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Location Tracking\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\\\\\\\\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\\\\\\\\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\\\\\\\\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Location Tracking Details\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\\\\\\\\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"This document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## QR Code Sharing\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- Display your own device ID as a QR code, copy it, or share via link or email.\\\\\\\\n- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\\\\\\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":67},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; Guide\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## App Navigation and Views\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9085,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"                  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"                  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"                  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"                  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The user reports seeing a double transition when selecting another device, which might involve two quick animation pushes. I’m considering that both the row NavigationLink and some tap gesture might lead to this, but DeviceRowView doesn’t use tap gestures in normal mode. The double navigation could be due to the NavigationLink to deviceID in the list and the iPhone_DeviceMapView’s onAppear setting lastOpenedDeviceID. The ghost itself is used to show how far the user has progressed towards a destination along the route. In the DeviceNavigationView, the &#96;progress&#96; is calculated with &#96;elapsed / expectedTravelTime&#96;. The ghost coordinate indicates the user's progress, located ahead of the device along the route.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":202,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"It's interesting that progress is calculated based on the elapsed time since the last device update—this means progress is used to move the ghost along the route, even though the user is the one actually moving. It seems like the ghost visualizes where the user would be if they were moving toward the device at the expected travel pace. \\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":247,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When progress is small but positive, I think I should focus on the distance near the route. The ghost point seems to be located near the device, moving back along the line as time passes, which means the user is moving towards the device based on the expectedTravelTime. I wonder if it makes sense to integrate actual speed into the computation instead of relying solely on expectedTravelTime. If the device speed is known and greater than zero, I could adjust the calculations accordingly.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":253,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I’m considering how we could adjust expected travel progress by adding a dynamic term related to the device's movement speed over time. The device might either be moving towards or away from the user. However, lacking heading information makes it tricky. I could heuristically assume a worst-case or best-case scenario. Without knowing user speed, it seems the goal is to refine the ghost marker to separate the predicted device position from the route. I might estimate the device's position based on its last two cached locations, but there's no history store to help.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":341,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I need to update all cache write calls in multiple files like iPhone_GroupMapView.swift and iPad_GroupMapView.swift, which means I'll have to edit those files directly. It would be good to create a helper, possibly in views/Common or Libraries. Following repository rules, logic should ideally be in managers, and perhaps a new tool for location/per route could go into Libraries. I’m leaning towards creating &#96;RouteGhostCalculator.swift&#96; in views/Common while ensuring it remains lightweight and follows project guidelines like copyright headers. It’s not user-facing, so no localization is needed here.\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-09-03_11-56Z-offscreen-arrows-ein-und-ausblenden.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":67,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| &#96;/// OffScreenDeviceArrow renders an arrow label at the screen edge pointing towards a device&#96; | L14 |\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-28_12-27Z-voiceover-für-die-gesamte-app-aktivieren.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":763,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I’m working with an xcstrings JSON file, and updating it by inserting entries at the right locations can be tricky, but I think it’s manageable. Then, I’ll run the necessary lints.\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-27_09-25Z-navigation-starten-bei-swipe-left-auf-devicerow.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1169,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I'm thinking that if we change the NavigationStack's id when the selection changes, it will reset the stack and dismiss any pushed navigation destinations. Although we already reset the id for iPad_DeviceMapView on updates, the NavigationStack itself stays the same. By setting the NavigationStack's id to something like .id(selection ?? lastSelectedDeviceID ?? \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"none\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), the stack will reset, which seems straightforward. Alternatively, I could track a navStackKey. I’m leaning towards using selection to simplify it. I wonder if keeping the original line navigationTargetDevice = nil might be a simpler solution for closing the navigation.\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-22_11-01Z-top-bar-transparent-on-ipad.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":118,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I'm exploring the new iPad's top Tab Bar, which might be a segmented control style for the TabView. The screenshot features a tint bubble navigation with options like \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Devices, Groups, QR-Code, Settings.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" The default &#96;TabView&#96; style usually shows at the bottom, but in iPadOS 18, it seems to be shifting towards a top sidebar navigation. It's interesting how this new design uses a compact, floating segmented control that could even be transparent. This fresh approach appears to enhance the top bar navigation visually!\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-22_10-27Z-prüfung-der-offscreen-statuskriterien.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":39,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| &#96;/// OffScreenDeviceArrow renders an arrow label at the screen edge pointing towards a device&#96; | L13 |\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":65,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| &#96;/// OffScreenDeviceArrow renders an arrow label at the screen edge pointing towards a device&#96; | L13 |\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":209,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"If the device is offscreen, I should be using the ray from the center to the device point for rotation. The arrow's rotation angle is based on this device point, and if that point is far off, the arrow points inward toward that direction. The user sees arrows pointing directly inward to the center when the calculated device point aligns with the screen center. I wonder if this is influenced by special logic in coordinate calculations or by clamping small spans during rotation? There's definitely a lot to consider!\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":221,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"The device screen point can sometimes end up far away from the center, which complicates intersection calculations. I wonder why the arrows point towards the screen center instead of outwards? It might be because the graphics are rotated inward. Users could think arrows should indicate offscreen targets, pointing outward. But if the map heading is temporarily set to zero, that could lead to arrows appearing in the wrong direction. It’s crucial to clear up these mixed signals about arrow placement!\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":224,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I’m considering cases where the arrow might inaccurately point towards the screen center. For instance, if the map heading is set to 180°, the device point could flip to the opposite side, misleading the intersection calculations. Another possibility is when the device point, despite being outside, is mistakenly perceived as inside due to numerical issues. This could lead to confusing orientations, like the arrows appearing inconsistent with the actual device locations. User expectations can clash with how the code interprets and displays these orientations!\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-22_10-17Z-offscreen-device-settings-anpassen.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":42,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| &#96;/// OffScreenDeviceArrow renders an arrow label at the screen edge pointing towards a device&#96; | L13 |\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-22_09-23Z-debug-outputs-with-ifdef-statements.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":202,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\" /// OffScreenDeviceArrow renders an arrow label at the screen edge pointing towards a device\\\\\\\"}]},{\\\\\\\"file\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-08-19_12-29Z-debug-offscreendevicearrow-rotation-issue.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"matches\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":436,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I noticed that the coordinateToScreenPoint function currently gives an unrotated screen point. For arrow rotation, it should aim towards the device point on the screen. However, I realized we need to adjust the intersectionPoint function to take dx and dy as parameters instead of recomputing them from the center.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":958,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I’m looking into animating the position changes of a component. To animate OffScreenDeviceArrow's position, we might need to use .animation on the computed position. position along a route, optionally weighting by known device speed.\\\\\\\\n/// If speed is provided (in m/s) and timestamp is available, the progress is adjusted from time\\\\\\\\n/// since last device update and capped to [0,1]. Falls back to MKRoute.expectedTravelTime otherwise.\\\\\\\\n/// Speed values below the threshold are ignored to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices.\\\\\\\\nstruct RouteGhostCalculator {\\\\\\\\n    /// Minimum speed threshold in m/s to consider device as moving.\\\\\\\\n    /// Values below this threshold are treated as GPS noise from stationary devices.\\\\\\\\n    /// Default: 1.5 m/s (5.4 km/h) - reasonable threshold to filter out GPS drift.\\\\\\\\n    static let speedThreshold: Double = 1.5 // m/s\\\\\\\\n    /// Calculates the ghost coordinate and polylines for completed/remaining segments.\\\\\\\\n    /// - Parameters:\\\\\\\\n    ///   - route: The MKRoute to traverse.\\\\\\\\n    ///   - deviceTimestamp: The last known timestamp of the remote device location.\\\\\\\\n    ///   - knownDeviceSpeed: Optional remote device speed in meters per second.\\\\\\\\n    ///   - userTimestamp: The last known timestamp of the local device location.\\\\\\\\n    ///   - knownUserSpeed: Optional local device speed in meters per second.\\\\\\\\n    ///   - now: Reference time (defaults to Date()).\\\\\\\\n    ///   - isRouteReversed: Whether the route is reversed (device at start vs end).\\\\\\\\n    /// - Returns: (donePolyline, todoPolyline, ghostCoordinate, progress [0,1]) or nil if cannot compute.\\\\\\\\n    static func ghost(for route: MKRoute, deviceTimestamp: Date?, knownDeviceSpeed: Double?, userTimestamp: Date?, knownUserSpeed: Double?, now: Date = Date(), isRouteReversed: Bool = false) -&gt; (MKPolyline, MKPolyline, CLLocationCoordinate2D, Double)? {\\\\\\\\n        guard route.distance &gt; 0 else { return nil }\\\\\\\\n        let totalDistance = route.distance\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\n        // Only use speeds above the threshold to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices\\\\\\\\n        let deviceSpeed = usableSpeed(knownDeviceSpeed)\\\\\\\\n        let userSpeed = usableSpeed(knownUserSpeed)\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\n        // Pick the fastest available speed; choose its corresponding timestamp for elapsed time\\\\\\\\n        let chosenSpeed: Double?\\\\\\\\n        let chosenTimestamp: Date?\\\\\\\\n        if let deviceSpeed, let userSpeed {\\\\\\\\n            if deviceSpeed &gt;= userSpeed {\\\\\\\\n                chosenSpeed = deviceSpeed\\\\\\\\n                chosenTimestamp = deviceTimestamp\\\\\\\\n            } else {\\\\\\\\n                chosenSpeed = userSpeed\\\\\\\\n                chosenTimestamp = userTimestamp\\\\\\\\n            }\\\\\\\\n        } else if let deviceSpeed {\\\\\\\\n            chosenSpeed = deviceSpeed\\\\\\\\n            chosenTimestamp = deviceTimestamp\\\\\\\\n        } else if let userSpeed {\\\\\\\\n            chosenSpeed = userSpeed\\\\\\\\n            chosenTimestamp = userTimestamp\\\\\\\\n        } else {\\\\\\\\n            chosenSpeed = nil\\\\\\\\n            chosenTimestamp = nil\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\n        let fallbackElapsed: TimeInterval\\\\\\\\n        if let deviceTimestamp {\\\\\\\\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(deviceTimestamp)\\\\\\\\n        } else if let userTimestamp {\\\\\\\\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(userTimestamp)\\\\\\\\n        } else {\\\\\\\\n            fallbackElapsed = 0\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\n        let distanceFromDevice: CLLocationDistance\\\\\\\\n        if let speed = chosenSpeed {\\\\\\\\n            if let ts = chosenTimestamp {\\\\\\\\n                let elapsed = max(0, now.timeIntervalSince(ts))\\\\\\\\n                distanceFromDevice = min(totalDistance, max(0, elapsed * speed))\\\\\\\\n            } else {\\\\\\\\n                // Without a timestamp we cannot project using speed; fall back to travel time\\\\\\\\n                let expected = route.expectedTravelTime\\\\\\\\n                let progress = expected &gt; 0 ? max(0, min(1, fallbackElapsed / expected)) : 0\\\\\\\\n                distanceFromDevice = totalDistance * progress\\\\\\\\n            }\\\\\\\\n        } else {\\\\\\\\n            // Fallback: use expectedTravelTime proportion if available (device appears stationary)\\\\\\\\n            let expected = route.expectedTravelTime\\\\\\\\n            let progress = expected &gt; 0 ? max(0, min(1, fallbackElapsed / expected)) : 0\\\\\\\\n            distanceFromDevice = totalDistance * progress\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n        // Ghost calculation should ALWAYS be from the device's perspective\\\\\\\\n        // The device is always at the start of its journey, regardless of route direction\\\\\\\\n        // When isRouteReversed = true: device at start of polyline, travels forward\\\\\\\\n        // When isRouteReversed = false: device at end of polyline, travels forward (backward along polyline)\\\\\\\\n        let splitDistance: CLLocationDistance\\\\\\\\n        if isRouteReversed {\\\\\\\\n            // Device at start, travels forward: split at distanceFromDevice from start\\\\\\\\n            splitDistance = max(0, min(totalDistance, distanceFromDevice))\\\\\\\\n        } else {\\\\\\\\n            // Device at end, travels forward from its position (backward along polyline)\\\\\\\\n            // Split at distance from start: totalDistance - distanceFromDevice\\\\\\\\n            splitDistance = max(0, min(totalDistance, totalDistance - distanceFromDevice))\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\n        guard let   "markdown": "import Combine\nimport Foundation\nimport MapKit\n\n/// Observes changes to the user's navigation progress and updates the overlay accordingly.\n/// \n/// This view model manages the state of navigation instructions and remaining distances,\n/// providing methods to advance through route steps and update the displayed information.\n/// It acts as the bridge between MapKit route data and the SwiftUI navigation overlay.\npublic final class NavigationOverlayViewModel: ObservableObject {\n /// The current navigation instruction to display in the overlay\n @Published public private(set) var instruction: NavigationInstruction?\n \n /// The remaining distance to the destination (may differ from instruction distance)\n @Published public private(set) var remainingDistance: Measurement?\n\n /// The MapKit route containing all navigation steps\n private let route: MKRoute?\n \n /// The preferred unit for distance measurements\n private let unit: UnitLength\n\n /// The index of the currently displayed route step\n private var currentStepIndex: Int\n\n /// Initializes the navigation overlay view model\n /// \n /// - Parameters:\n /// - route: Optional MapKit route containing navigation steps\n /// - unit: The preferred unit for distance measurements (defaults to meters)\n public init(route: MKRoute? = nil, unit: UnitLength = .meters) {\n self.route = route\n self.unit = unit\n self.currentStepIndex = 0\n \n // Initialize with the first step if a route is provided\n if let route {\n updateInstruction(stepIndex: currentStepIndex, route: route)\n }\n }\n\n /// Advances the displayed instruction to the next step in the route\n /// \n /// Moves to the next navigation step and updates both the instruction\n /// and remaining distance. This is typically called when the user\n /// completes the current maneuver.\n public func advance() {\n guard let route else { return }\n let nextIndex = currentStepIndex + 1\n updateInstruction(stepIndex: nextIndex, route: route)\n }\n\n /// Updates the instruction to a specific step index\n /// \n /// Allows jumping to any step in the route, useful for scenarios like\n /// rerouting or when the user manually selects a different step.\n /// \n /// - Parameter index: The index of the route step that should be displayed\n public func update(step index: Int) {\n guard let route else { return }\n updateInstruction(stepIndex: index, route: route)\n }\n\n /// Updates the view model with a completely new instruction\n /// \n /// This method is used when providing custom navigation instructions\n /// that don't come from a MapKit route, such as manual directions\n /// or external navigation data.\n /// \n /// - Parameter instruction: The instruction to display\n public func update(with instruction: NavigationInstruction) {\n self.instruction = instruction\n self.remainingDistance = nil\n }\n\n /// Updates only the remaining distance shown in the overlay\n /// \n /// Allows updating the distance information without changing the\n /// current instruction or symbol. Useful for real-time distance\n /// updates during navigation.\n /// \n /// - Parameter distance: The distance to display\n public func updateRemainingDistance(to distance: Measurement) {\n self.remainingDistance = distance\n }\n\n /// Updates the instruction and remaining distance for a specific route step\n /// \n /// Internal method that handles the core logic of updating the view model\n /// state when advancing through route steps. Validates the step index\n /// and updates both instruction and remaining distance.\n /// \n /// - Parameters:\n /// - stepIndex: The index of the step to display\n /// - route: The MapKit route containing the steps\n private func updateInstruction(stepIndex: Int, route: MKRoute) {\n guard route.steps.indices.contains(stepIndex) else { return }\n currentStepIndex = stepIndex\n instruction = NavigationInstruction.from(route: route, currentStepIndex: stepIndex, unit: unit)\n remainingDistance = calculateRemainingDistance(from: stepIndex, route: route)\n }\n\n /// Calculates the total remaining distance from a specific step to the end of the route\n /// \n /// Sums up the distances of all steps from the given index to the end of the route,\n /// converting the result to the preferred unit.\n /// \n /// - Parameters:\n /// - index: The starting step index\n /// - route: The MapKit route containing the steps\n /// - Returns: The total remaining distance as a measurement\n private func calculateRemainingDistance(from index: Int, route: MKRoute) -&gt; Measurement {\n let remainingMeters = route.steps[index...].reduce(0) { partialResult, step in\n partialResult + step.distance\n }\n return Measurement(value: remainingMeters, unit: UnitLength.meters).converted(to: unit)\n }\n}\n"
}

MKRoute, before index: Int) -&gt; Int? {\n guard index &gt; 0 else { return nil }\n var i = index - 1\n while route.steps.indices.contains(i) {\n if route.steps[i].polyline.pointCount &gt;= 2 {\n .slightLeft: return NSLocalizedString(\"Slight left\", comment: \"Default instruction text for slight left turn\")\n case .left: return NSLocalizedString(\"Turn left\", comment: \"Default instruction text for left turn\")\n case .sharpLeft: return NSLocalizedString(\"Sharp left\", comment: \"Default instruction text for sharp left turn\")\n case .uTurn: return NSLocalizedString(\"Make a U-turn\", comment: \"Default instruction text for U-turn\")\n case .arrive: return NSLocalizedString(\"Arrive\", comment: \"Default instruction text for arrival\")\n case .cross: return NSLocalizedString(\"Cross\", comment: \"Default instruction text for crossing\")\n case .tunnel: return NSLocalizedString(\"Through tunnel\", comment: \"Default instruction text for tunnel traversal\")\n case .bridge: return NSLocalizedString(\"Over bridge\", comment: \"Default instruction text for bridge traversal\")\n case .stairs: return NSLocalizedString(\"Use stairs\", comment: \"Default instruction text for stairs\")\n case .escalator: return NSLocalizedString(\"Use escalator\", comment: \"Default instruction text for escalator\")\n }\n }\n\n /// Computes a turn symbol using the signed angle between previous and current step polylines.\n /// Positive angles are treated as left turns, negative as right turns.\n private static func geometryTurnSymbol(previous prev: MKPolyline, current cur: MKPolyline) -&gt; NavigationInstruction.Symbol? {\n guard let v1 = lastNonZeroSegmentVector(of: prev),\n let v2 = firstNonZeroSegmentVector(of: cur) else { return nil }\n let angle = signedAngleDegrees(between: v1, and: v2)\n let absAngle = abs(angle)\n\n if absAngle &lt; 15 { return .straight }\n if absAngle &lt; 45 { return angle &gt;= 0 ? .slightLeft : .slightRight }\n if absAngle &lt; 120 { return angle &gt;= 0 ? .left : .right }\n if absAngle &lt; 170 { return angle &gt;= 0 ? .sharpLeft : .sharpRight }\n return .uTurn\n }\n\n private static func firstNonZeroSegmentVector(of polyline: MKPolyline) -&gt; (dx: Double, dy: Double)? {\n let count = polyline.pointCount\n guard count &gt;= 2 else { return nil }\n var coords = Array(repeating: kCLLocationCoordinate2DInvalid, count: count)\n polyline.getCoordinates(&amp;coords, range: NSRange(location: 0, length: count))\n for i in 0..&lt;(count - 1) {\n let a = MKMapPoint(coords[i])\n let b = MKMapPoint(coords[i + 1])\n let dx = b.x - a.x\n let dy = b.y - a.y\n let len = hypot(dx, dy)\n if len &gt; 1e-6 { return (dx / len, dy / len) }\n }\n return nil\n }\n\n private static func lastNonZeroSegmentVector(of polyline: MKPolyline) -&gt; (dx: Double, dy: Double)? {\n let count = polyline.pointCount\n guard count &gt;= 2 else { return nil }\n var coords = Array(repeating: kCLLocationCoordinate2DInvalid, count: count)\n polyline.getCoordinates(&amp;coords, range: NSRange(location: 0, length: count))\n for i in stride(from: count - 2, through: 0, by: -1) {\n let a = MKMapPoint(coords[i])\n let b = MKMapPoint(coords[i + 1])\n let dx = b.x - a.x\n let dy = b.y - a.y\n let len = hypot(dx, dy)\n if len &gt; 1e-6 { return (dx / len, dy / len) }\n }\n return nil\n }\n\n private static func signedAngleDegrees(between v1: (dx: Double, dy: Double), and v2: (dx: Double, dy: Double)) -&gt; Double {\n // atan2 of cross and dot gives signed angle from v1 to v2\n let cross = v1.dx * v2.dy - v1.dy * v2.dx\n let dot = v1.dx * v2.dx + v1.dy * v2.dy\n let radians = atan2(cross, dot)\n return radians * 180.0 / .pi\n }\n}\n\n// MARK: - Multilingual instruction parsing and geometry helpers\n\nprivate extension NavigationInstruction {\n static func symbolFromLocalizedInstruction(_ text: String) -&gt; NavigationInstruction.Symbol? {\n let t = text.lowercased()\n\n // U-turn\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.uTurnTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .uTurn }\n\n // Arrive\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.arriveTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .arrive }\n\n // Start of route\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.startTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .start }\n\n // Feature-based: tunnel/bridge/escalator/stairs/cross (checked before turns)\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.tunnelTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .tunnel }\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.bridgeTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .bridge }\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.escalatorTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .escalator }\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.stairsTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .stairs }\n if LocalizedManeuverTokens.crossTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) }) { return .cross }\n\n // Modifiers\n let slightTokens = LocalizedManeuverTokens.slightTokens\n let sharpTokens = LocalizedManeuverTokens.sharpTokens\n\n // Left/Right\n let leftTokens = LocalizedManeuverTokens.leftTokens\n let rightTokens = LocalizedManeuverTokens.rightTokens\n\n let isLeft = leftTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) })\n let isRight = rightTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) })\n let isSlight = slightTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) })\n let isSharp = sharpTokens.contains(where: { t.contains($0) })\n\n if isLeft {\n if isSharp { return .sharpLeft }\n if isSlight { return .slightLeft }\n return .left\n }\n if isRight {\n if isSharp { return .sharpRight }\n if isSlight { return .slightRight }\n return .right\n }\n\n // Unrecognized\n return nil\n }\n}\n"

Integrated NavigationOverlayKit into the device navigation view so the top overlay appears only in user→device mode, stays in sync with route/location changes (including cached routes), and clears when navigation stops or reverses. I also added a polyline distance helper for step matching and updated the feature docs and changelog.

Key wiring in `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView` for the overlay stack:
```
368:392:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift

                topOverlayStack
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
                scaleBarView()
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {
                compassView()
            }
    }
    
    @ViewBuilder
    private var topOverlayStack: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 8) {
            navigationOverlayContent
            topOverlayContent
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private var navigationOverlayContent: some View {
        if let navigationOverlayViewModel, !isRouteReversed, route != nil {
            NavigationOverlayView(viewModel: navigationOverlayViewModel, alignment: .top)
        }
    }
```

Route/step syncing and overlay lifecycle:
```
1083:1117:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift
    private func refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() {
        guard !isRouteReversed, let route else {
            navigationOverlayViewModel = nil
            lastOverlayStepIndex = nil
            return
        }
        navigationOverlayViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: navigationOverlayUnit())
        lastOverlayStepIndex = nil
        updateNavigationOverlayStep()
    }

    private func updateNavigationOverlayStep() {
        guard !isRouteReversed,
              let route,
              let navigationOverlayViewModel,
              let location = locationManager.currentLocation else { return }
        guard let stepIndex = closestStepIndex(for: route, to: location.coordinate) else { return }
        if stepIndex != lastOverlayStepIndex {
            navigationOverlayViewModel.update(step: stepIndex)
            lastOverlayStepIndex = stepIndex
        }
    }

    private func closestStepIndex(for route: MKRoute, to coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D) -> Int? {
        let point = MKMapPoint(coordinate)
        var bestIndex: Int?
        var bestDistance: CLLocationDistance = .greatestFiniteMagnitude
        for (index, step) in route.steps.enumerated() {
            guard let distance = step.polyline.closestDistance(to: point) else { continue }
            if distance < bestDistance {
                bestDistance = distance
                bestIndex = index
            }
        }
        return bestIndex
    }
```

Polyline distance helper used for step matching:
```
158:179:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/Common/Map/MapHelpers.swift
extension MKPolyline {
    func closestDistance(to point: MKMapPoint) -> CLLocationDistance? {
        guard pointCount > 0 else { return nil }
        let points = self.points()
        if pointCount == 1 {
            return point.distance(to: points[0])
        }
        var closest = CLLocationDistance.greatestFiniteMagnitude
        for index in 0..<(pointCount - 1) {
            let start = points[index]
            let end = points[index + 1]
            let distance = distanceFrom(point, toSegmentBetween: start, end)
            if distance < closest {
                closest = distance
            }
        }
        return closest.isFinite ? closest : nil
    }
```

miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## App Navigation and Views\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\\\\\\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96;, and &amp;#96;iPhone_SettingsView&amp;#96;.\\\\\\\\n- &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\\\\\\\\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &amp;#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&amp;#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Location Tracking\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\\\\\\\\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\\\\\\\\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\\\\\\\\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Location Tracking Details\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\\\\\\\\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"This document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**.
